transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-05
Start: 15:00 EST
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Samira Ortiz (Redwood AE), Ethan Cole (Redwood SE), Maya Lin (Redwood CSM), Priya Nair (Head of Compliance - Crownridge), Jordan Vale (CISO), Liam Chang (Platform Eng), Sofia Ortega (Devops)

Summary:
Quick discovery to map where Crownridge can host inference, what data classifications must remain in-region, and what audit/evidence they need for internal/regulatory reviews. Focus on tradeoffs between Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, and Private VPC options and the logging/retention constraints for EU personal data + US financial records.

Topics:
- Data residency requirements (EU-only personal data, US-financial records)
- Audit log retention, access patterns, redaction needs
- Customer-managed keys, KMS/HSM, escrow concerns
- Network egress and cross-border operator access
- Pilot scope: private VPC vs dedicated pool for sensitive workloads

Action items (light recap at top): see action_items field

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samira Ortiz: hey everyone thanks for taking time. quick intro, im Samira, i'm the AE here. with me is Ethan, our solutions engineer, and Maya for success. who do we have from Crownridge?
[00:12] Priya Nair: this is Priya, head of compliance. hey. Jordan on for security, Liam for platform, and Sofia handles our infra.
[00:18] Jordan Vale: hey, morning.
[00:21] Ethan Cole: great, thanks. goal today is to understand the boundaries: what data can leave the EEA, what must stay, what your auditors want to see in logs, and then recommend Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
[00:35] Liam Chang: yes, our current ask - we have two buckets. PII of EU clients must never leave EU data centers. Second bucket is US payment records, which are allowed in the US but require 7 years retention and strict access auditing.
[00:51] Sofia Ortega: and one more, we have internal telemetry that is allowed broadly but must be sanitized before any external vendor sees it.
[01:02] Samira Ortiz: good, that maps to a couple of Redwood patterns. Hosted API (Redwood hosted) is easiest but may not satisfy EU-only hard residency for PII unless you use our region-locking feature. Dedicated gives you reserved capacity in a region and stronger isolation. Private (VPC or on-prem) replaces the public control plane with your private control plane so nothing leaves your VPC except the metrics you opt in for.
[01:28] Priya Nair: when you say "region-locking" can you be specific? we need technical guarantees for audit. the contract team will ask for language.
[01:36] Ethan Cole: sure - region-locking is an option where requests from an EU tenant are routed exclusively to EU-hosted instances and logs that include request payloads stay in the EU logging cluster. i should caveat that for Hosted we still maintain multiregion control plane metadata for billing, but payload-level data is stored only in-region if you pick EU region. i'll send the exact SLA language. (a little stutter) but note that for the strictest customers we recommend Private VPC so control plane plane metadata also can be kept on-prem.
[02:05] Jordan Vale: okay, what about KMS? we need customer-managed keys and key custody - can't have keys exported or stored by the vendor.
[02:13] Ethan Cole: we support customer-managed keys via a KMS integration. for Dedicated and Private you can bring your own KMS, and we can integrate with major cloud KMS or HSM. for Hosted we offer envelope encryption but customers sometimes ask for a KMS proxy. there is also an option for key escrow in special enterprise contracts.
[02:32] Priya Nair: that escrow option is interesting - our legal team flagged escrow because of regulatory fallback in insolvency cases. do you have references?
[02:38] Samira Ortiz: we have a documented key-escrow process for larger deals. i'll include references in the pack. it's part of our enterprise addendum.
[02:46] [Speaker 1]: um sorry interrupt, does Redwood retain full transcripts in logs by default?
[02:50] Maya Lin: defaults vary. by default we log request IDs, model used, latency and token counts. payload logging is off unless explicitly enabled for debug or audit. for customers with compliance needs we recommend enabling payload logging with retention rules and encryption tied to your KMS.
[03:08] Sofia Ortega: so we would want payload logs for our audit team, but retention must be 7 years for US financial, and EU PII must be 2 years then deletion. can Redwood support per-route retention policies?
[03:20] Ethan Cole: yes, we have per-route retention TTLs in Dedicated and Private. Hosted can support it too but it requires a custom agreement to map retention to tenant intents; again Private gives you the most direct control.
[03:30] Liam Chang: what about operator access? we do not want any vendor engineer to be able to access PII.
[03:35] Jordan Vale: exactly.
[03:36] Samira Ortiz: understood. for Dedicated we provide role-based access and we can restrict vendor operator roles from data-plane access. for Private, operator access is under your control - Redwood engineers only have access if you grant it (jumpbox or support session). all access sessions are logged and we can integrate with your SIEM.
[03:53] Priya Nair: do you have SOC2 or HIPAA attestation?
[03:57] Ethan Cole: yes SOC2 Type II and a HIPAA BAA is available for customers handling PHI. i'll attach the latest report. per your legal question earlier, the SOC2 report describes controls around access, key management and logging.
[04:08] Priya Nair: good. for our auditors, we also need immutable audit trails - can logs be tamper-evident?
[04:15] Ethan Cole: we can stream logs to your SIEM or to write-once storage with signed checksums. for Private deployments we can sign logs using your HSM. there may be a small integration effort.
[04:28] [00:04:30] Jordan Vale: can we simulate an operator access event for our SOC team? like a mock breach or mock support session to show the chain?
[04:36] Samira Ortiz: absolutely, we typically include that in a pilot runbook. Ethan, can you run through the pilot outline?
[04:41] Ethan Cole: sure. pilot steps: 1) define a sample workload and dataset (we'll sanitize PII), 2) deploy Private VPC instance in EU region, 3) configure customer-managed KMS, 4) run perf baseline and capture logs to your SIEM, 5) execute a support session with full audit trail. expected 2-3 weeks.
[04:58] Liam Chang: two to three weeks sounds fine. do you have back-of-envelope numbers for latency differences between Hosted and Private? we worry about 50-100 ms increases adding up.
[05:08] Ethan Cole: generally, Dedicated in-region often matches Hosted latency since it's the same infra but reserved. Private can be slightly higher depending on your networking and if you're doing VPC NAT or siting on-prem. typical delta is 10-40 ms per request for small models; above that, it depends on batching and sequence length. i'll include a small table and an example script to measure it.
[05:26] Priya Nair: on retention and deletion chains - if a user requests erasure under GDPR, can you guarantee deletion from caches, logs, and backups?
[05:34] Maya Lin: we support deletion hooks at the tenant level and we have KV cache evict APIs. backups are handled with retention windows; for Hosted we can coordinate certified deletion with timestamps for audits; Private gives you absolute control. for backups we can set a policy to not include certain classes, or to use shorter retention.
[05:52] Sofia Ortega: what about cross-border operator access - sometimes we have vendors outside EU that need to run jobs. is there support for operator geofencing?
[05:59] Ethan Cole: yes, we can restrict operator admin consoles to specific IP ranges and MFA enforced. for Dedicated we can restrict vendor access to a region and for Private you can handle access with your identity provider. we integrate with SSO/SAML, and you can enforce conditional access.
[06:14] Jordan Vale: curious about logging redaction - can Redwood redact PII at capture time? we prefer redaction before logs leave our environment.
[06:21] Ethan Cole: we offer pre-ingest redaction rules (regex based and ML-assisted). you can do client-side redaction too. for strict customers we push a sidecar that removes PII before payload is sent to Redwood, or we can run in your VPC so logs never leave.
[06:36] [00:06:40] Priya Nair: this is a bit operational - what's your process for responding to subpoenas?
[06:42] Samira Ortiz: legally, Redwood only responds to requests that are valid and we notify customers if their data is requested unless prohibited. with Private deployments the legal exposure is mostly under your purview. we'll add the legal contact in the next steps pack.
[06:55] Liam Chang: can you also share example CAN I cheat the word — uh — regional routing policies? in particular, fallback when EU capacity is exhausted. we don't want PII to be routed to US even temporarily.
[07:07] Ethan Cole: fallback policies are flexible. defaults allow fallback to compatible model variants in other regions for availability; however we can set strict policies that avoid cross-region failover for tenants with hard residency constraints. when strict_no_fallback is set, requests will queue or return 429s. we can also do synchronous fan-out to a secondary EU-only standby.
[07:28] Sofia Ortega: queueing is better than leaking data. we'll prefer queueing or degraded mode.
[07:33] Samira Ortiz: understood. i'll ensure the pilot config uses strict_no_fallback for EU-PII routes.
[07:38] [00:07:40] Priya Nair: what evidence will you provide for auditors? we need a mapping: control -> artifact (e.g., access logs / role assignments / KMS policy).
[07:46] Ethan Cole: we'll provide an evidence pack: SOC2 report, HIPAA BAA (if applicable), role assignment exports, signed log excerpts, KMS policy examples, and a deployment diagram showing where keys and logs live.
[07:57] Jordan Vale: can you also include a sample incident response runbook for data-plane incidents?
[08:01] Maya Lin: yes, we have an incident runbook template plus playbook for support escalations. we'll include that.
[08:06] [00:08:10] Liam Chang: slightly tangential - are there cost differences between Dedicated and Private? we want to estimate TCO.
[08:13] Samira Ortiz: Dedicated is priced as reserved capacity: you pay for GPU pools, predictable and usually cheaper per token compared to burst-hosted. Private has additional setup and infra charges and can be higher upfront but gives more control. we'll include a TCO worksheet for your specific traffic profile.
[08:28] Priya Nair: about data destruction proof - our auditors sometimes ask for signed deletion certificates. do you issue those?
[08:33] Ethan Cole: yes for enterprise contracts we can issue deletion certificates with signed timestamps, and if you're on Private we can have your HSM sign the event.
[08:41] Sofia Ortega: small operational question - will Redwood ever index or use our prompts for training?
[08:46] Samira Ortiz: by default we do not use customer prompts for model training; we have an opt-in program for telemetry/quality improvements. for regulated customers we enforce an opt-out. we'll note that in contract language.
[08:58] [00:09:00] Priya Nair: perfect. ok last stretch - we want to run a mini-pilot: EU VPC tenant that processes anonymized PII, customer-managed KMS, retain logs 2 years for EU routes and 7 years for US routes, and mock operator access exercises. can Redwood commit to that timeline?
[09:13] Ethan Cole: yes, that's what our typical pilot looks like. i'll own the perf baseline and mock exercises. Samira will send the contractual and compliance artifacts.
[09:21] Jordan Vale: will you need any signed NDA or data processing addendum before pilot?
[09:25] Samira Ortiz: we have a standard DPA and NDA for pilots. i'll circulate them after this meeting.
[09:30] Priya Nair: one more small ask - we need a diagram showing where telemetry flows during normal ops, and a variant where telemetry flow is entirely internal (no external vendor telemetry).
[09:38] Ethan Cole: noted. we'll provide two diagrams.
[09:41] [00:09:50] Maya Lin: recap next steps: samira sends docs and DPA, ethan prepares pilot runbook + perf scripts, crownridge provides infra inventory and final list of data classes. schedule pilot kickoff.
[09:55] Samira Ortiz: sounds good. thanks everyone. any final questions?
[09:58] Priya Nair: none from compliance. thanks.
[10:00] Jordan Vale: no, thanks.
[10:02] Liam Chang: thanks, appreciate it.
[10:04] Sofia Ortega: bye.

End of call.

Meeting recap (auto-generated, imperfect):
- Crownridge needs EU-only residency for PII and 7-year retention for US financial records.
- Redwood options: Hosted (easy, may need contract addendum), Dedicated (reserved capacity, region isolation), Private (VPC/on-prem, max control).
- Key asks: customer-managed keys, strict_no_fallback routing for EU PII, per-route retention TTLs, tamper-evident logs, operator geofencing, deletion certificates.
- Pilot agreed: Private VPC in EU, sample sanitized dataset, KMS integration, perf baseline, mock operator session and audit evidence.

References mentioned / to be shared:
- SOC2 Type II report (latest)
- HIPAA BAA template
- Pilot runbook template and perf script
- Region-by-region hosting diagram and retention SLA

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker mislabels and automatic timestamps; some technical terms may be garbled (e.g., "K V cache" instead of KV cache).
